title: Not in Peter's orchestra; Navy day job and parade pay
summary: Low pay made him stop; he worked at the Navy and took days off for funerals and parades with the Excelsior at about thirty dollars.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you play much with your cousin Pete? Uh. Did you play much with your cousin Pete? Pete? Did you play in his band?

I played in his, I played in a brass band with him, but I never played, I never played in the orchestra with him. No. Charlie played in the orchestra with him, see? Of course, like I say this, at that time, why I stopped fooling with it, didn't care about it, because you couldn't make a living that music in them days, because the low salary that you got playing. What did you do then?
What kind of job did you have? Huh? What kind of job did you have? How did you make your life?

Well I was waking down at the Navy at that time. Oh. Yes, waking at the government. Of course I could get off, go play funerals and parades like that, because I had days up there that I could take off and go play parades and things like that. We used to play the longshoremen parades, lab-a-dee parades, all like that, the excelsa brass band. But that was hard, you'd make about, about thirty dollars a man on that job, but you're walking so much, all day long. I played one lab-a-dee parades and was stalled up for a whole week, couldn't walk.
